```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

The TileScope analysis engine is a Python package that consumes pairwise
CSV inputs of the form `x, y, gene1, gene2, roi_id`. This R package
provides one bridge function that produces those CSVs from a Seurat
spatial object.

## Load

```{r load}
library(TileScope)
library(Seurat)
```

## Prepare a Seurat object

Any Visium Seurat object with (i) spatial coordinates readable through
`GetTissueCoordinates()`, (ii) a normalized-expression layer, and
(iii) a metadata column holding your ROI or spatial-cluster labels
will work. For example:

```{r load_seurat}
object <- readRDS("path/to/sample_1.rds")
DefaultAssay(object) <- "Spatial"
```

## Export pairwise CSVs

`extract_data_from_seurat_to_csv()` writes one CSV per gene pair to
`out_path`. The `input_data` argument dispatches on its type:

* a character vector: every pairwise combination of the listed genes;
* a list of length-2 character vectors: only those explicit pairs;
* a named list of gene vectors: each name is scored via
  `Seurat::AddModuleScore()` and pairs of scores are written.

```{r export_gene_pairs}
extract_data_from_seurat_to_csv(
  seurat_obj   = object,
  sample_id    = "sample_1",
  assay        = "Spatial",
  layer        = "data",
  metadata_col = "spatial_cluster",
  input_data   = c("GFAP", "PDGFRA", "MKI67"),
  out_path     = "tilescope_inputs/"
)
```

## Run the Python analysis engine

Install `tilescope` in a Python environment, then invoke the CLI on
each generated CSV:

```bash
tilescope tilescope_inputs/sample_1_expression_data_GFAP_PDGFRA.csv \
  --profile standard \
  --output results/sample_1/GFAP_PDGFRA/
```

The output directory contains the canonical CSVs (correlations,
enrichments, consensus, Moran, cross-grain sensitivity), the
diagnostic PDFs, and an `analysis_report.html` summary.

Alternatively, drive TileScope directly from R via `reticulate`; see
`python/tilescope/api/R_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md` for the exact call.

## Join results back to Seurat

```{r join_back}
roi_result <- read.csv("results/sample_1/GFAP_PDGFRA/roi_correlations.csv")
roi_key    <- as.character(object@meta.data$spatial_cluster)
object$tilescope_correlation <- roi_result$corr_obs[
  match(roi_key, as.character(roi_result$roi_id))
]
```
